findings.claim: The recorded major blind tell — D is the ONLY option that mentions the wind, against a stem whose whole frame is 'before the wind drops' — was never remediated and is never dispositioned anywhere in the shipping unit, yet pedagogy returned MINOR_FIXES.
findings.evidence: Stem: 'What is said about the open joints before the wind drops?'. Options: A 'Every joint above the opening is running...' (no wind), B 'The brick is still soaking up the rain, so nothing has reached the tray yet.' (no wind), C 'Nothing comes out of them, which usually means the tray was laid without stop ends.' (no wind), D 'Whatever the tray has caught stays on it, because the wind presses in at those joints.' — the sole wind-bearing option, and the sole option whose state is indexed to the wind. verdicts/verdicts-gstem.jsonl already recorded this at severity major: "The stem's own framing 'before the wind drops' additionally makes D the only wind-referencing option, a mild lexical-overlap tell... Blind pick D." A byte-diff of candidates/ -> candidates-corrected/ -> candidates-final/ shows the stem and all four option texts are IDENTICAL across all three stages: the only passage edit was inserting a comma after 'While the wind is still on the wall', and the only other edit was a rationale rewrite. The shipped rationale audits exactly two blind heuristics — "neither 'pick the qualified answer' nor 'strip the absolutes' locates the key" — and generator_meta.hedge_balance_note concludes "Both blind heuristics - pick-the-hedged and strip-the-absolutes - fail on this set"; neither text mentions stem-lexis matching. ASSEMBLY.md's 'Flags carried to the fleet and V-FINAL' lists elf-b16-003 only under 'Declared shortfalls' (fk_grade 8.7, two-phrase probe); grep for 'G-STEM' / 'blind pick' / 'disposition' across ASSEMBLY.md and BRIEF-ADDENDUM.md returns no G-STEM disposition at all.
findings.why: The pedagogy stage's stated remit is whether a test-wise student can score without reading. A stem-to-option lexical bridge that no other option shares is exactly that failure, an independent blind gate graded it major with an explicit 'Blind pick D', and the shipping unit carries neither a text fix nor a written disposition. The rationale's blind-heuristic section is therefore incomplete in a way that reads as a clean bill of health it has not earned. Cheap fix, no key change: put the wind into at least one distractor (e.g. B 'The brick is still soaking it up while the wind blows, so nothing has reached the tray yet.') or de-lexicalise the stem ('before the storm eases').

findings.claim: The trap label for B does not name the actual trap, and the rationale contradicts itself one sentence later. B is not a reversal or a mis-ordering — it preserves the passage's own order and merely arrests it one stage early.
findings.evidence: Rationale: 'B = reversed sequence: it puts the wetting of the brickwork and the arrival of water on the tray in the wrong order, holding that the outer skin is still absorbing and that the tray is therefore still dry.' generator_meta.engineered_traps repeats it: 'B = reversed/mis-sequenced mechanism'. But B reads 'The brick is still soaking up the rain, so nothing has reached the tray yet.' — brick-wetting BEFORE water-on-tray, which is precisely the passage's order ('the outer skin of brick wets through' ... 'The water that gets past it runs down into the cavity, onto a tray'). Nothing is reversed and nothing is out of order. The rationale's own next sentence gives the correct diagnosis and thereby contradicts the label: 'because a lag between rain and leak is what most readers assume.' A lag trap and a reversed-order trap are different misconceptions.
findings.why: The rationale is the teaching payload. A student told that B fails because it 'puts... in the wrong order' can check B against the passage, find the order identical, and correctly conclude the explanation is wrong — which teaches the wrong diagnostic move. Integrated review's own criterion is that trap labels name the actual trap and that the rationale not contradict itself; this line fails both. Fix is one word: 'B = premature stage / lag' in the rationale and in engineered_traps.

findings.claim: Unanchored pronoun in 'The lull is when it lets go.' — the sentence the rationale leans on to fix the timing that defeats distractor A. Across sentences 3-6 the pronoun 'it' carries four different referents, twice clashing inside a single sentence; the language stage edited that exact sentence chain (comma insertion) and left the referent chain untouched.
findings.evidence: Passage sentences 3-6: '...the outer skin of brick wets through, as the specification assumes it will [it = the outer skin]. The water that gets past it [it = the outer skin] runs down into the cavity, onto a tray bedded in over the opening, which discharges it [it = the water] through the open joints. While the wind is still on the wall, it [it = the wind] pushes in at those same joints, and the tray holds what it [it = the tray] has collected. The lull is when it lets go. [it = the tray]'. In the last of these, 'it' has no local antecedent; the topical subject of the sentence is 'The lull', a property of the wind, and the wind-reading yields a tautology (the lull IS the wind letting go), so the reader must reach back past two intervening referents to the tray. The rationale depends on this sentence: 'the discharge belongs to a different moment (\'The lull is when it lets go\')'. The language stage's only recorded change to the unit was inserting a comma into the immediately preceding sentence ('on the wall, it pushes in'), i.e. it worked inside this exact chain. Same-sentence clashes: 'gets past it ... discharges it' (outer skin / water) and 'it pushes in ... what it has collected' (wind / tray).
findings.why: ELF is read by L2 test-takers under time pressure, and the whole item turns on the during/after contrast that this sentence carries. G-REGISTER already flagged the same sentence for its 'telegraphic, elliptical' rhythm at minor severity; the referential side of it went unrecorded. Not key-breaking — D remains the single best answer, and each pronoun is recoverable on a second pass — but a native-expert language pass that touched this chain should have named it. Fix: 'The lull is when the tray lets go.'
